rawContent: Okay, that L'Oreal/Winona commercial confused me. I thought i was watching something serious about the #MeToo movement and then - BAM! - hair product commercial. Way too extra just to shill shampoo.

@girlsreallyrule I am, however, into shaming her for her comments that the women coming out now in the #MeToo movement actually wanted sex at the time but are pretending they didn't now because they regret their actions.

@thesideofmyface @MrRighTNoW_818 I don't think this is a #MeToo moment, but I certainly think it's something that needed to be said. More young girls need to understand that it's okay to say "NO." Loudly. Clearly. And more men need to understand how to treat women in physical encounters.

@angelicabastien Honestly, it's the open of the paragraph that disgusts me more than the close. It's clear from the start that the author is not someone who takes the #MeToo movement or women in general seriously. We're all just spoiled little girls making shit up, apparently.
